texts.preamble: Ram Baboo vs State Of U.P. on 2 February, 2024 Author: Samit Gopal Bench: Samit Gopal High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad ?Neutral Citation No. - 2024:Ahc:18031 Court No. - 74 Case :- Criminal Revision No. - 5149 of 2009 Revisionist :- Ram Baboo Opposite Party :- State of U.P. Counsel for Revisionist :- B.G. Yadav,Rajendra Kumar Yadav Counsel for Opposite Party :- Govt. Advocate Hon'ble Samit Gopal,J. 1.
texts.facts: 5. The facts of the case are that R.K. Lavania, the Food Inspector found the revisionist on 07.03.2000 at about 11.45 a.m. at Udal Chowk while he was selling milk without license. The food Inspector introduced himself and purchased 750 ml of milk from the revisionist by giving Rs. 9 for sample and then kept in three bottles in equal quantity after mixing 20% formalin for preserving it which was then sent to the public analyst for chemical analysis who vide his report being report no. A.G.0259 dated 06.07.2000 reported it to be adulterated. The complainant then took sanction from the C.M.O. concerned and filed a complaint against the revisionist/accused. In the trial court the complainant R.K. Lavania, the Food Inspector was examined as P.W.-1, Ravi Shankar Tripathi, Food Clerk was examined as PW-2. The accused/revisionist in his statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C. denied the prosecution case and stated of false implication. The appeal was preferred against the same which came to be dismissed after which the present revision has been filed against both the impugned judgement and orders.
texts.arguments: 6. Learned counsel for the revisionist argued that R.K. Lavania, the Food Inspector was examined as PW-1 under Section 244 Cr.P.C. and states of taking sample of milk from the revisionist. It is further argued that the notice under Section 13(2) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 has not been received by the revisionist. It is argued that there is nothing on record to show that the same as has been sent by the Food Inspector has been received by the revisionist and as such valuable right of the accused/revisionist safeguarding his interest is violated. To buttress the arguments learned counsel has placed the judgement of the Apex Court in the case of Vijendra vs. State of Uttar Pradesh: (2020) 15 SCC 763 (para-14 and 15) and Narayan Prasad Sahu vs. The State of Madhya Pradesh: (2022) 1 SCC 87 (para-5, 6, 8 and 9). While further elaborating the arguments it is argued that as per Section 13(2) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954, report of food analyst has to be sent within a period of 10 days from the date of receipt of the same, but in the present case the said report has been alleged to be sent to the revisionist on 18.10.2001 which is after about six months of the sample being tested which clearly frustrates the purpose and valuable rights of a person to get the sample of the same retested by the Central Food Laboratory. It is argued that the Apex Court has, in no uncertain terms, in the judgement of Vijendra case (supra) held that failure of the trial court to take into consideration that no evidence was brought on record to indicate that the report which has been claimed to be dispatched, was actually sent or delivered for the purpose of further reference to the Central Food Laboratory, if the accused is dissatisfied with the said report. It is further argued that even the trial court has failed to take note of the said fact and also to record a finding that there is evidence to show that the said report has been received at the end of the accused/revisionist. The said safeguard is provided to the accused under Section 13(2) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954. It is argued that the present revision thus deserved to be allowed. Ram Baboo vs State Of U.P. on 2 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/142107011/ 2 7. Learned counsel for the State opposed the prayer and arguments and argued that the trial court has given cogent reasons for convicting the revisionist.
